DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 75 s. 2021 10 June 2021 HON. LEONARDO DE LUNA ABELLA Municipal Vice-Mayor Catanauan, Quezon totalcatanauan@outlook.com Dear Vice-Mayor Abel!a: This in reference to your ietters dated 19 January 2021 and 19 February addressed to Regional Director seeking this opinion regarding the following, and we quote: a. Is the budget of Sangguniang Bayan requires approval from the Local Chief Executive (LCE) on the basis of new government forms issued by the Department of Budget and Management? b, Does the Municipal Vice Mayor need to have a request from the LCE on matters in Sangguniang Bayan, especially on the implementation or use of Personnel Services, MOOE and Capital Outlay? c. Is the demolition of a building, previously used as Association of Barangay Captain Hall located inside the municipal property which was constructed on staggered basis and not entered into book as asset of LGU, requires Sangguniang Bayan approval? d. Can the LCE solely allow or approve the construction of building inside the government lot without the approval or concurrence from the Sangguniang Bayan? The budget may be from National or Provincial Fund? Foremost, allow us to lay the bases of local government units' budget pursuant to Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), specifica!!y Section 317, 318 and 319 thereof, to wit: SECTION 317. Submission of Budget Proposals by Heads of Departments or Offices. — (a) Each head of department or office shall submit a budget proposal for his department or office to the local chief executive on or before the fifteenth (15th) of Juiy of each year: Provided, That

the budget proposal of each department of office shall be categorized under either economic, social or general services: Provided, further, That each service shall be covered by the budget of at least one (l) department or office of the local government unit concerned. The said budget proposai Shail be prepared in accordance with such policy and program guidelines as the local chief executive concerned may issue in conformity with the local development plan, the budgetary oeilings presoribed by the loc.al finance oommitteew and the general requirements prescribed in this Title. (b) Budget proposals of departments or offices shall be divided into two (2) primary categories, namely: the current operating expenditures and the capital outlays. Such budget proposals shall contain the following information: (I) Objectives, functions, and projects showing the genera! character and relative importance of the work to be accomplished Oi the setvices IO be rendered; and the cost thereof; (2) Organizational charts and staffing patterns indicating the list of plantilla positions with their corresponding salaries, and proposals for reclassification of positions and salary changcs, as well as the creation of new positions with their proposed salary grade, duiy supported by proper justification; (3) Brief description of the functions, projects and activities for the for project and activity, and the nature of work to be performed, including the objects of expenditure for each function, project and activity; (4) Relation of the work and financial proposals to approved local development plans; (5) Estimated current operating expenditures and capital outlays comparative data fOf iasttWO (2) preceding, C;Uitent, and ensuing fiscal years; and (6) Accomplishment reports for the last two (2) preceding and current fiscal years. SECTION 318. Preparation of the Budget by the Local Chief Executive. — Upon receipt of the statements of income and expenditures from the treasurer, the budget proposals of the heads

of departments and offices, and the estimates of income and budgetary ceilings from the local finance committee, the local chief executive shall prepare the executive budget for the ensuing fiscal year in accordance with the provisions of this Title. Thc local chief executive shall submit thc said executive budget to the sanggunian concerned not later than the sixteenth (16th) of October of the current fiscai year. Faiiure to submit such budget on the date prescribed herein shall subject the local chief executive to such criminal and administrative penalties as provided for under this Code and other applicable laws. SECTION 319. Legislative Authorization of the Budget. — On or before the end of the current fiscal year, the sanggunian concerned shall, through an ordinance, the annual budget of the local government unit for the ensuing fiscal year on the basis of the estimates of income and expenditures submitted by the local chief executive. In sum, the budget of a local government unit comprises of budget proposals from the heads of departments and offices and estimates of income and budgetary ceilings from the Local Finance Committee (LFC). Said proposals from heads of departments/offices shall be in accordance with the approved Annual Investment Plan (AIP), guidelines and spending ceilings as specified in the Budget Cali, and other general requirements prescribed under Section 317 of the Local Government Code. Upon receipt of the foregoing, the iocai chief executive (LCE) shaii prepare the executive budget for the ensuing year and submit the prepared executive budget to the sanggunian concerned. In turn, the sanggunian shall enact, through an appropriation ordinance, the annual budget of the iocai government unit for the ensuing fiscal year. The Appropriation Ordinance shaii contain, among others, the expenditure program by Department/Office/Unit, to include the Office of the Sangguniang Bayan, which comprises: (1) mandate, vision, mission and organizational outcome (2) new appropriations of PPA, expense class, and object of expenditures, and (3) special provisions, if any. Thereafter, the Secretary to the Sanggunian shall forward the Appropriation Ordinance enacted by the sanggunian and duly certified by the Presiding

Officer to the LCE for approval, in which case, he/she shall affix his/her signature on every page thereof. Considering the above discussion and in reply to the first query, since the budget of the Sangguniang Bayan forms part of the budget of the local government unit of Catanauan, Quezon, the same shall be signed by the LCE, through the Appropriation Ordinance enacted by the Sangguniang Bayan. in connection thereto, may we invite your attention to the 2016 Budget Operations Manual for Local Government Units, specifically LBA Form No. IA ("Checklist on Documentary and Signature Requirements for the Annual Budget'), for reference on who shaii be the signatory of every documents relating to LGU's budget. Further, in view of Article 426 of the implementing Rules and Regulations of the LGCi which empowers the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) and the Commission on Audit (COA) to promulgate Budget Operations Manual for LGUs and for the DBM to promulgate administrative issuances, we hereby recommend that the comments/inputs of the DBM regarding the new government forms issued, be solicited. With respect to the second query, we answer in the negative. It is worthy to note that in the preparation of the annual budget of a local government unit (LGU), each department or office, including the Office of Sangguniang Bayan, Sha!! submit a budget proposa! for his department or office to the local chief executivel, which shall be incorporated and considered in the appropriation ordinance. Clearly, the Office of the Sangguniang Bayan, being the legislative body of the LGU, has its own budget as proposed and included in the annual budget. Thus, tho Municipal Vice-Mayor nood not obtain thc permission nor request the local chief executive to use the budget allocated for the Office of the Sangguniang Bayan. Regarding the third issue, this level has reservation since the source of fund for the construction of the Association of Barangay Captain (ABC) Hall was not stated, and in fact, the same has not been entered as asset of the LOU. 1 Section 317, Republic Act No. 7160

Nonetheless, Section 18 of the LGC states that LGUs has the authority to acquire, develop, lease, encumber, alienate, or otherwise dispose of real or personal property heid by them in their proprietary capacity and to apply their resources and assets for productive, developmental, or welfare purposes, in the exercise or furtherance of their governmental or proprietary powers and functions and thereby ensure their development inlo seif-reiiant communities and active participants in the attainment of national goals. in connection thereto, Section 447 of the same Code provides the powers, duties, and functions of Sangguniang Bayan with respect to municipal properties, to wit: Section 447. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. - (a) The sangguniang bayan, as the legislative body of the municipality, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the municipality as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall: (I ) Approve ordinances and pass resolutions necessary for an efficient and effective municipal government, and in this connection shall: (x) Provide a mechanism and the appropriate funds therefor, to ensure the safety and protection of all municipal government property, public documents, or records such as those relating to property inventory, land ownership, records of births, marriages, deaths, assessments, taxation, accounts, business permits, and such other records and documents of public interest in the offices and departments of the municipal government; (2) Generate and maximize the use of resources and revenues for the development plans, program objectives and priorities of the municipality as provided for under Section 18 of this Code with particular attention to agro-industrial development and countryside growth and progress, and relative thereto, shall: (v) Appropriate funds for the construction and maintenance or the rental of buildings for the use of the municipality and, upon the majority vote of all the members of the sangguniang bayan, authorize the municipal mayor to lease to private

parties such public buildings held in a proprietary capacity, subject to existing laws, rules and regulations; (vi) Prescribe reasonable limits and restraints on the use of property within the jurisdiction of the municipality: EVidently, the LGC speaks only ot municipal properties or properties which are held by the municipality in its propriety capacity. However, although LGUs can dispose real properties, there is no specific mention if such disposition includes demolition. Furthermore, pursuant to Section 447, the Sangguniang Bayan can on!y exercise its powers and authority over municipal properties. But since, and to reiterate, the source of fund for the construction of ABC Hall was not stated, this Department is constrained to provide for a definitive opinion on the matter as the subject property cannot be clearly regarded as a municipal property. With respect to the last issue, the answer thereto would depend if there is a contract for the construction of the building. However, the general rule stand in the affirmative pursuant to Section 22(c) of the LGC, which was discussed in DILG Legal Opinion No. 12, Series of 2015, citing the case of Hon. Gabriel Luis Quisumbing et.al. vs. Hon. Gwendolyn F. Garcia, et.al. The Supreme Court's ruling therein was summarized by the Commission on Audit (COA) in Memorandum No. 2010-014, dated 22 April 2010, to wit: "The decision of the Supreme Court in the above case clearly indicated the instances when prior approved or authorization by the sanggunian is necessary and not necessary in incurring expenses or entering into a contract by the local chief executive officer in behalf of the !oca! government unit. This may be summarized as follows: I. The disbursement of funds for the items enumerated under Section 323 of RA 7160 does not require approval or authorization by the sanggunian. However, such list of items being exclusive, as evidenced by the use of the word "only" under the said provision, contractual obligation which wcrc included in thc previous year's annual and supplemental budgets cannot be disbursed by the local government unit. 2. Even if the transaction is covered by the enumeration of items under Section 323 of RA 7160, new contracts thereon to be entered into by the require the prior authorization Of sanggunian. In the gase of the regularly enacted budget:

1. Ifthe project and cost of capital outlay is specifically described and the details thereof are sufficiently provided, or the purchase of goods and services and maintenance operating expenses, such that all that the local chief executive needs to do is to execute the contract, no further approval or authorization by tho sanggunian is required. 2. if the project is described in generic terms, such as infrastructure projects, inter-municipal works, drainage and sewerage, flood control, and irrigation system project, reclamation project or roads and bridges, a for eveo,' specific project with the prior approval authorization of the sanggunian is required. 3. If the purchase of goods and services are neither specified nor encompassed within the regular persona/ services and maintenance operating expense, a specific contract for every such purchase with the prior approval or authorization of the sanggunian is required. " Based on the foregoing, in the case of regularly enacted budget, prior approval or authorization of the sanggunian is required: (1) for a contract for every specific project if the project is described in generic terms, such as infrastructure projects, inter-municipal waterworks, drainage and sewage, flood control, and irrigation system project, reclamation projects, or roads and bridges; (2) for a specific contract for every purchase of goods and services that are neither specified nor encompassed within the regular personal services and maintenance operating expense. On the other hand, no further approval or authorization by the sanggunian is required if the project and cost of a capital outlay or the purchase of goods and services and maintenance operating expense is specifically described and the details thereof are sufficiently provided in the appropriations ordinance. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: GAN, CESO iii Underse for Local Government
